response.output:
Use this sequence, ordering serializers from least coupled to most dependent:

| Unit | Change | Check before advancing | Rollback |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0. Baseline | Record current state, dependencies, and representative fixtures for all four serializers; preserve unrelated work. | Existing contract tests pass. | No migration changes yet. |
| 1. Compatibility | Introduce the new contract alongside the old path, if required. | Old fixtures remain readable; new-format round trips pass. | Restore the old path. |
| 2–5. One serializer per unit | Migrate each serializer with its affected consumers and fixtures. Combine serializers only when their contract requires atomic movement. | Verify round trips, malformed inputs, backward compatibility, and dependent consumers. | Switch that unit back to the retained implementation. |
| 6. Integration | Exercise all four together. | Cross-serializer exchanges and end-to-end flows pass against the final state. | Reverse affected units in dependency order. |
| 7. Cleanup | Remove compatibility code after the rollback window closes. | Full contract and integration checks pass. | Restore compatibility code. |

Stop at any failed check before advancing dependent work. If migration writes persistent data, retain compatible readers or a verified restoration path before enabling those writes.

Skill followed: principle-sequence-verifiable-units.
